title: One Tangent Intersection: ln x and the Line x - 1
originalTopic: Tangency and the count of intersections
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The graphs of y = ln x and y = x - 1 appear to touch rather than cross near x = 1. Determine how many intersection points they have and explain the geometric relationship between the two curves at that point.
finalAnswer: \text{Exactly one intersection, at } (1, 0); \quad y = x - 1 \text{ is tangent to } y = \ln x

steps.title: Solve the intersection equation
steps.explanation: Substitution shows x = 1 works, giving the point (1, 0).
steps.why: An exact candidate found by inspection is what the rest of the analysis must confirm or rule out.

steps.title: Prove it is the only one
steps.explanation: The only critical point is x = 1, and since h is concave down everywhere on (0, infinity), that critical point is a global maximum with h(1) = 0. Hence h(x) <= 0 for every x > 0, with equality only at x = 1.
steps.why: A global maximum of exactly zero means the two graphs never separate, which proves there is no second intersection.

steps.title: Match the slopes to confirm tangency
steps.explanation: Both curves pass through (1, 0) with slope 1, so the line is the tangent line to the logarithm at that point and the inequality ln x <= x - 1 holds for all x > 0.
steps.why: Equal value and equal slope at a shared point is exactly the definition of tangency, which explains why the plot shows touching instead of crossing.
